extracted.intended_audience: health sciences librarians with intermediate literature searching experience
extracted.subtask_description: A professional development workshop that trains health sciences librarians to plan, conduct, and communicate systematic reviews via an online Canvas course plus two days of live instruction. Participants should already have intermediate literature-searching skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop purpose / learning goal
rubrics_metrics.description: The systematic reviews workshop is designed to teach librarians how to plan, conduct, and communicate the results of a systematic review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad learning goal framing what the course aims to achieve for participants: foundational and practical skills across planning, execution, and reporting of systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended participants
rubrics_metrics.description: We welcome health sciences librarians with intermediate literature searching experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies target audience and baseline experience level expected for successful participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite skills/knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants are expected to be familiar with boolean operators, advanced search features, controlled vocabulary, and field tags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific search skills are assumed; lack of familiarity may impede learning and hands-on exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accreditation / continuing education credits
rubrics_metrics.description: This workshop is accredited for 20 Medical Library Association continuing education credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates formal CE recognition and credit value for professional credentialing/record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall format
rubrics_metrics.description: The systematic reviews workshop starts with an asynchronous online course in Canvas, followed by 2 days of live instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hybrid structure: self-paced preparatory modules plus concentrated in-person/ live sessions to apply and extend online learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Canvas course structure and workload
rubrics_metrics.description: The online Canvas course provides 10 online learning modules and activities designed to establish a foundation of the systemic reviews process, with topics relevant for health science librarians. You should expect to commit 8–10 hours total to this online component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies module count, purpose (foundation), audience relevance, and expected time commitment for planning purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live instruction content and teaching methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Live instruction covers the key steps and processes of conducting systematic reviews through a combination of lectures, discussion, hands-on exercises, and group presentations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes pedagogical methods (lecture, discussion, hands-on, group presentation) and that live sessions focus on applying key steps/processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration / notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign up to receive email notifications about upcoming offerings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Logistical guidance for interested participants to stay informed about future workshop dates and registration; separate page/link provided for registration and fees details.
